MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 19, 2023
  VARIO US TELECONFERENCE LOCATIONS
  5:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Skophammer called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dane Skophammer; Vice Chair Cayley Jenner; and Commissioners
  Georgia Goldfarb, Suzanne Guldimann, and Alicia Peak

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Chris Orosz, Recreation
  Supervisor; and Loren Davis, Recreation Coordinator

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Skophammer led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Goldfarb moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Community Services Director Riesgo reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on September 15, 2023.

ELECTION OF CHAIR AND VICE CHAIR

  Chair Skophammer opened the floor for nominations for Chair.

  Commissioner Guldimann nominated Vice Chair Jenner to serve as Chair, and
  Commissioner Goldfarb seconded the nomination.

  Commissioner Peak nominated Chair Skophammer to remain Chair.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of September 19, 2023
  Page 2 of 12

  The question was called, and Commissioners Goldfarb, Guldimann, Vice Chair
  Jenner, and Chair Skophammer voted for Vice Chair Jenner to serve as Chair.
  Commissioner Peak voted for Chair Skophammer to remain Chair.

  Vice Chair Jenner was elected to serve as Chair.

  Chair Jenner opened the floor for nominations for Vice Chair.

  Commissioner Goldfarb nominated Commissioner Guldimann to serve as Vice
  Chair.

  Commissioner Skophammer nominated Commissioner Peak to serve as Vice Chair.

  The question was called, and Commissioners Goldfarb, Guldimann, Peak, and
  Chair Jenner voted for Commissioner Guldimann to serve as Vice Chair.
  Commissioner Skophammer voted for Commissioner Peak to serve as Vice Chair.

  Commissioner Guldimann was elected to serve as Vice Chair.

ADMINISTRATION OF OATH OF OFFICE TO NEWLY ELECTED CHAIR AND VICE
CHAIR

  Community Services Director Riesgo administered the oath of office to Chair
  Jenner and Vice Chair Guldimann.

ITEM 1  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  Bill Sampson was not present at the time of the meeting.

ITEM2  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Vice Chair Guldimann moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the June 20, 2023 Parks
  and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of September 19, 2023
  Page 3 of 12

  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in August 2023.

ITEM3  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM4  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Recreation Program Selection Process and the Swim Team Program
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the Program Selection Guidelines; 2) Review
  the management operations of the Malibu Community Pool; and 3) Provide
  feedback to staff regarding the swim team program.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Vice Chair Guldimann, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  that program submittal deadlines were formulated to allow time for scheduling and
  contract processing. She stated the City did not have any significant issues with the
  Malibu Aquatics Foundation since the pandemic.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated the Malibu Aquatics Foundation signed the contract agreement before the
  completion of the Malibu Marlins Swim Club application submittal. She
  summarized the Request for Proposals (RFP) process, contractor compensation,
  and contractor application process. She stated that the prospective contractors'
  experience in program production, marketing, outreach, and understanding of the
  community's needs are considered in the selection process. She stated that no
  official City policy governed the determination of independent instructor contracts.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo
  confirmed that there were very specific requirements for contractors, and if
  expectations were not met, the situation was remedied, or future contracts were not
  offered. She stated that timely bids were considered for similar programs, but an
  established contractor would likely be selected. She stated the new prospective
  contractor information would be kept on file. She stated staff may work with the
  instructor to modify their program so it was not duplicative. She stated that
  feedback from some swimming participants indicated a need for a more competitive
  program.

  Robert Brinkmann stated there were misrepresentations in the staff presentation and
  requested that the Commissioners contact him for clarification. He stated that he
  was a founding member and current treasurer of the Malibu Marlins Swim Club.
  He stated most of their members formerly belonged to the Seawolves Swim Club
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of September 19, 2023
  Page 4 of 12

and members felt they had no voice in the decisions made by the Malibu Aquatics
Foundation. He stated they based their new club on transparency and
accountability. He requested the Commission's support of the Malibu Marlins
Swim Club. He stated that they were led to believe by City staff that they would
have access to the swimming pool if they registered enough swimmers, but the City
changed direction and some swimmers were forced to join the Seawolves for their
physical education requirement. He stated that a proposal to accept their application
next year was a way to get rid of them. He stated that the assertion that the
Seawolves were in place with the City since 2012 was incorrect, as the Secretary
of State website showed they were defunct, and the Malibu Aquatics Foundation
was established during the COVID-19 pandemic.

David Shoshan stated that he was the parent of two children who planned to join
the Malibu Marlins Swim Club. He stated that the Malibu Marlins Swim Club
submitted an instructor application in early August 2023 and indicated agreement
with Mr. Brinkmann's comments. He stated that the Malibu Marlins Swim Club
offered the swimming community a voice in decisions, whereas the Malibu
Aquatics Foundation did not. He encouraged the Commission's support of the
Malibu Marlins.

Roko Belie expressed gratitude to City staff and the Commission. He stated that his
daughter was the captain of the Blue Team and was blindsided and destabilized by
the termination of the Seawolves coach but felt forced to stay with the Seawolves
to continue training. He stated the bigger concern was that the swimmers and
parents had no say in the Malibu Aquatics Foundation's programming and coaching
decisions. He requested the Commission's assistance finding lanes for the Malibu
Marlins.

Lawrence Meyers stated that he has been involved in youth sports for 40 years and
that all participants were members who had a voice. He stated that according to the
bylaws, each member helped elect a Board of Directors that handled business
affairs such as contracting with the City. He stated that the swim lanes should be
shared by both clubs, similar to the management of shared field space for Malibu
Little League and Pony League. He stated that by December 1, 2023, there should
be coordination between the two swim organizations to coexist.

Jennifer Galan advocated for equal access to the pool for all community members,
especially those unable to participate in the Masters Program due to scheduling
conflicts in the morning hours. She stated that the Malibu Marlins should have fair
access to resources, especially because the newly formed club aligned with a
community-oriented swim experience. She stated that Erik Ran's coaching style
resonated with her and that he was approachable and easygoing, which motivated
her and her children. She stated that when she had proposed wearable technology
to the Malibu Aquatics Foundation to help swimmers be more competitive, her
proposal was denied without discussion or consideration. She stated that there was
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of September 19, 2023
  Page 5 of 12

a need for fairness, inclusivity, democracy, and a choice in coaching style in the
City's swim club offerings.

Erik Ran stated that he was the swim coach for the Malibu Marlins and that he
appreciated everything the Commission did for the community. He stated that he
was terminated as coach of the Seawolves for not being competitive enough. He
provided a background of his swimming career, track record of his service and
stated that he changed careers and moved to Malibu four years prior to coach and
mentor the swimming community and during the COVID-19 pandemic he worked
without a day off for over one and a half years growing the program from 22 to 96
swimmers. He stated that he created a special bond with the children and trust with
the parents and broke 78 team records and four high school records. He stated that
upon his termination, the community supported him and started the Malibu Marlins
Swim Club with more than 50 members requesting access to the pool from 6:00
p.m. to 7:15 p.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays and from 4:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. on
Fridays.

Joe Sichta stated that the Malibu Seawolves started as a non-profit organization and
later became the Malibu Aquatics Foundation, which had been the swim team
vendor since 2012. He stated the Malibu Aquatics Foundation used all its revenue
to provide City programs, which included Aqua Aerobics, Masters, and the
Seawolves Swim Team. He stated that during the Woolsey Fire and pandemic, their
volunteer Board of Directors sourced grants and funding to keep programs running.
He stated that they had 58 swimmers registered for Fall and their first swim meet
was held in Camarillo and had a great turnout. He refuted the newspaper report that
they padded their numbers with non-swimmers. He stated that their new coach and
Pepperdine University trained coaching staff provided great momentum to their
expanding program. He stated that making the Malibu Marlins a vendor would
undermine the City's own program and would be disruptive to Seawolves' practices
and unfair to the new coaching staff. He stated that they had two new Board
members, and that according to the nonprofit's bylaws, swimmers were not
members, and Board members were accountable to the City. He stated the Board
agreed that if the Malibu Marlins were given swim time, the Malibu Aquatics
Foundation would not provide services to the community.

Macloud Shoshan, former Seawolves member and current Malibu Marlins member,
stated that Coach Ran was highly regarded that a whole new swim team was created
for him to lead, and requested access to the pool in the afternoons.

Bill Sampson stated that the public was not privy to the details of Erik Ran's
termination, as it was a personnel matter. He stated that many of the same good
people were involved in the program since 2012. He stated that he assisted with
youth swimming programs over the years and that a program was not built by
tearing down one another. He suggested those that wanted to swim with Mr. Ran
to continue attending the morning swimming sessions. He stated it could be difficult
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of September 19, 2023
  Page 6 of 12

to attain a quorum with membership run organizations and that the pool was too
small to have two coaches from different clubs training swimmers.

Ingrid Shoshan stated that she emphatically endorsed a democratic organization and
that the swimmers were left in the dark and heartbroken about Coach Ran's
termination. She stated Coach Ran was positive and competitive. She stated that it
was not always about winning or losing or getting a record, but that it was important
participants were happy and felt good about their performance as they strived to
become stronger and better. She stated that the Malibu Marlins Swim Club was
formed for Coach Ran to be given the position of head coach. She stated that of the
58 swimmers in the Seawolves, some of those swimmers were doing so under
duress, to qualify for their Independent Study Program credits. She requested that
the Malibu Marlins Swim Club be granted swim time in the afternoon for those
who could not make it in the morning so they would be able to become better
swimmers, teammates, and human beings.

Sue Murphree stated that her children had been on the Seawolves swim team since
they were eight and nine years old and were now sixteen and asked everyone in the
meeting to listen to the voices of the 58 swimmers who signed up and continued to
swim with the Seawolves. She stated that they were passionate swimmers in support
of the decisions made by the Malibu Aquatics Foundation on their behalf to change
the head coach, who was terminated for cause, the details of which were not
publicly known. She stated that there was no time available for the Malibu Marlins
Swim Club and that the decision of the long-time swimmers to remain with the
Seawolves was made for a reason.

Commissioner Goldfarb stated that from the information provided, it appeared the
Malibu Marlins Swim Club did not offer all the programs that the Malibu Aquatics
Foundation provided and was concerned about the continuation of those programs.

In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
stated that the schedule was at capacity and the City needed to ensure all programs
had pool time; such as lap swim, free swim, and water polo. She stated lap
swimmers shared the pool with the Seawolves swim team and confirmed that an
attempt to accommodate the Malibu Marlins would result in the displacement of
the lap swimmers.

Recreation Coordinator Davis stated the pool was utilized for several programs
simultaneously and scheduling involved coordination of the 13-lane pool, within
the two-and-one-half hour time allotment each weekday during the school year.

In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
stated that the organization's Board of Directors were accountable for meeting
minimum enrollment, adequate insurance, and ensuring swimmers were in the USA
Swimming Program. She stated City staff did not have a seat on their Board and
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of September 19, 2023
  Page 7 of 12

did not attend meetings unless it was to provide information. She stated that youth
sports organizations such as American Youth Soccer Organization (A YSO) and
Malibu Little League (MLL) Boards voted on key positions, such as President,
which served as the City's point of contact for the season.

Commissioner Peak stated that her children participated in MLL, but she never
voted on Board members. She stated there were decisions made she disagreed with,
but she did not get a say in those decisions. She stated the Boards for each
organization would never make everybody happy with their decisions and felt it
was inaccurate to say nobody had any issues with A YSO or MLL decisions.

Commissioner Skophammer stated that people may have taken issue with decisions
made by the A YSO and MLL Boards, but no one from either organization said they
needed to be disbanded because it was not democratic.

Commissioner Goldfarb stated that Mr. Sampson seemed to have some experience
on the matter and that both styles of nonprofit governance were acceptable. She
stated that she was not sure that raising the undemocratic specter was legitimate,
although she understood why participants would want a say in the selection of their
coach, the fact that the Malibu Aquatics Foundation had a different process did not
make it unacceptable.

Vice Chair Guldimann stated that those issues were not relevant to whether the
Commission would act to facilitate the second team's access to the swimming pool.
She stated that they had every right to apply for use of the pool, but it did not mean
they were going to get access. She stated they did not submit their application in
time for the fall season, but they could submit it for the winter season, and then the
Community Services Department would decide. She stated that she did not
appreciate the Commission and the City being called undemocratic, but understood
emotions ran high and letters to the editor or posts on social media went out while
people were angry, but should not be considered in the Commission's decisions.
She stated that there were very limited resources and the best fit for the entire
community needed to be considered in facility use allocations. She stated that a new
community pool could allow for additional programming and encouraged those
who wanted more swim programs to advocate for a new swimming pool. She stated
the Commission would do everything in their power to be fair and facilitate the
application process, in the same way as any other applicant. She stated that it was
not the Commission's role to decide if anybody was right or wrong; they were there
to hear the community's concerns and help ensure the community received the use
of the Parks and Recreation Department resources.

Commissioner Skophammer stated that it sounded like the Malibu Marlins Swim
Club submitted their paperwork on time, but the application was not considered
because the Malibu Aquatics Foundation already submitted their application and
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of September 19, 2023
  Page 8 of 12

  signed the contract for the Fall Session. He stated there should be a selection
  process that made sense for the community.

  Commissioner Peak clarified that the deadline for the Fall Session was June 1, 2023
  and the Malibu Marlins Swim Club's application was submitted after the deadline.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated if it would take one year to create a selection
  process, it would take too long for the Malibu Marlins Swim Club's application to
  be considered.

  Vice Chair Guldimann questioned whether it was their responsibility to facilitate
  the Marlins Swim Club outside of the current process or their responsibility to
  publish the deadlines and require applicants to play by the rules. She stated that she
  was open to a second swim program, but if the submission deadline was not met,
  the applicant could apply when the window opened again. She stated that it was
  unfortunate, and she realized people felt passionately about the issue, but she was
  not sure anything was in their power to do but encourage them to apply again.

  Commissioner Peak thanked the public speakers and stated that it was a very
  difficult decision and what was learned rpost from the situation was the need for a
  new community pool.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated that should the Commission form an ad hoc committee, it could explore
  various options. She stated the committee could meet with each organization to
  discuss their needs and ways the City and the Commission should proceed in the
  application process.

  Commissioner Peak stated that she did not think there was a solution in this
  instance. She stated that hearing both sides, she felt the two swim programs could
  not coexist.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated the
  City did not have enough lifeguards over the age of 18 for the extended pool hours.
  She stated that morning and late evening pool time requests should be directed to
  the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District, and she did not know the
  District's arrangements for lifeguards.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, she stated that even if the City could
  provide a lifeguard over the age of 18 after 8:30 p.m. on weekdays and weekends,
  she did not know if those times would suit the Malibu Marlins.

MOTION  Commissioner Peak moved, and Chair Jenner seconded a motion to create an ad
  hoc committee consisting of Commissioners Peak and Skophammer to meet, at
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of September 19, 2023
  Page 9 of 12

  minimum, quarterly to review program guidelines, selection process, recommend
  adjustments, and report changes to contractors back to the Commission.

  The Commission discussed the motion.

  Vice Chair Guldimann offered to replace Commissioner Peak on the Earth Friendly
  Management Policy group to allow her time to serve on the new ad hoc committee.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

B.  Sports Field Allocation and Community Use Agreements
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the sports field allocation process; 2) Review
  the Community Use Agreement requirements; and 3) Provide feedback to staff
  regarding field allocation.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
  confirmed that the officers of both A YSO and MLL were elected by their Board of
  Directors and that the elected organizations President was the City's point of
  contact. She clarified that Community Use Agreements, such as those with A YSO
  and MLL were partnerships rather than instructor contract agreements.

  Commissioner Peak stated that volunteers serve on the A YSO and MLL Boards,
  and if there were more volunteers than open positions, there would be a vote, but
  that had not happened in recent years.

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated that there was no facility use cost to
  the City for A YSO and MLL to use Malibu Bluffs Park because the City owned the
  park. She stated that the City pays facility use fees to the School District to use the
  swimming pool. She stated to recover some expenses, the City needed to contract
  with an instructor to generate revenue. She stated participant fees are split 70% to
  the instructor and 30% to the city.

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated that any 50l(c)(3) nonprofit organization
  would be eligible for the Group One rental rate tier for Malibu Bluffs Park.

  Commissioner Peak stated that there was a substantial fee reduction for 50l(c)(3)
  nonprofit organizations and that there should be a requirement that the organization
  provided adequate benefit to the community.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  that an item could be brought back for discussion of the facility rental fee groups.
  She stated that commercial use of Malibu Bluffs Park was prohibited, but it was
  challenging to penalize those who were misusing the park. She stated City
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of September 19, 2023
  Page 10 of 12

  employees at the Michael Landon Center could request people to leave but could
  not issue a citation. She stated that finding a solution for misuse of the park required
  a discussion with the City Attorney's office and City Manager.

  Chair Jenner opened the floor to public comment.

  Bill Sampson commended Commissioner Peak for her service to the community
  and reminded the public about driving safety.

  Sue Murphree stated she would provide information on the formation of the Malibu
  Aquatics Foundation Board of Directors.

  Chair Jenner closed public comment.

  Commissioner Peak stated that the City would have a field space conflict with
  AYSO and the newly formed soccer organization, Views. She stated that the City
  should work with contractors that acted in good faith and followed the rules.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Commission directed staff to bring back an item to discuss the
  development of a process for monitoring compliance with the City's policies that
  would be factored into future allocation of facility rental space.

ITEM6  STAFF UPDATES

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz provided an update on the Charmlee Wilderness Park
  Full Moon Hike and a new partnership with Pepperdine University in connection
  with the Earth Friendly Management.

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on afterschool programs,
  Tiny Tot Olympics, Temporary Skate Park maintenance, and Permanent Skate
  Park.

ITEM7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Peak thanked staff for their work on the swimming pool allocation
  matter. She inquired if the farmers market could be contracted out to other providers
  and if it was the Parks and Recreation Commission's purview. She stated that she
  would like to place the Snack Shack project on the agenda.

  In response to Commissioners Peak and Skophammer, Community Services
  Director Riesgo stated that an item to discuss the Snack Shack would be on the
  October 24, 2023 Regular meeting agenda.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of September 19, 2023
  Page 11 of 12

Commissioner Skophammer indicated support for an item to discuss the fee
schedule for the parks. He thanked everyone for their work on the Snack Shack and
swimming pool allocation matter. He stated that the creation of a new pool would
help prevent future scheduling conflicts.

Chair Jenner stated that a new pool would help the swimming community with their
common goal of adequate pool time to avoid program disruption. She stated
Commissioners Peak and Skophammer would do a great job on the newly formed
program ad hoc committee. She also offered to replace Commissioner Peak on the
Earth Friendly Management Group if Commissioner Guldimann could not attend
the meetings. She supported discussing the Snack Shack item at the Regular
meeting on October 24, 2023, and stated the permanent skate park design was
beautiful.

In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated the
goal was to take the permanent skate park project to the Environmental Review
Board in November 2023 and have the Planning Commission hearing scheduled
before the end of the year.

In response to Chair Jenner, Vice Chair Guldimann stated that she would be grateful
if Chair Jenner could be on the Earth Friendly Management Working Group. She
stated that she was glad that a new Chair and Vice Chair were elected and thought
it was healthier for the Commission if everyone had a chance. She stated that a new
community swimming pool and multipurpose field would reduce the strain on
resources. She stated that during the recent Chili Cookoff, there were vehicles
parked under the Ioki family tree. She requested staff to install cones around the
tree when the property was rented for events.

In response to Vice Chair Guldimann and Chair Jenner, Community Services
Director Riesgo stated that barricades were placed around the tree as a condition of
use for the property, and staff would look into compliance.

Commissioner Goldfarb requested the ad hoc committee to address field and pool
resource allocation. She stated that there were multiple concerns regarding the
farmers market.

In response to Commissioner Goldfarb and Peak, Community Services Director
Riesgo stated the farmers market was not under the purview of the Parks and
Recreation Commission, but the City Manager's office was working with the
operators to address concerns raised by the public.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

None.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of September 19, 2023
  Page 12 of 12

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 8:22 p.m. , Commissioner Goldfarb moved, and Chair Jenner seconded a motion
  to adjourn the meeting. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.
